findings.title: The new downsize definition replaces the existing width/height API
findings.body: Ruby does not overload methods by argument count: this second definition of `self.downsize` replaces the definition above it. Existing calls passing width, height, and options now raise ArgumentError; calls passing just width and height treat the height as `opts` and fail when `optimize` accesses `opts[:allow_animation]`. Preserve both call forms in a single method or give the dimensions-based method a separate name so existing image-downsizing callers continue to work.

findings.title: Oversized animated GIF uploads lose their animation even when it is allowed
findings.body: The downsizing call passes the multipart tempfile path, which normally has no `.gif` extension. `OptimizedImage.optimize` selects its animated implementation only when the input path ends in `.GIF`, so `allow_animation: true` does not preserve animation here. The regular conversion reads only `from[0]` and overwrites the uploaded file with its first frame. Consequently, uploading an oversized animated GIF permanently discards its animation despite `allow_animated_thumbnails` being enabled. Detect the format independently of the temporary filename or use an appropriately suffixed working file.

findings.title: Keep the configured size limit for non-image attachments
findings.body: The unconditional 10 MB limit also applies to attachments, although the new server-side downsizing applies only to images. This removes enforcement of `max_attachment_size_kb` in the client: attachments above a smaller configured limit are submitted only to be rejected by the server, while attachments allowed by a configured limit above 10 MB can no longer be uploaded through the UI. Apply the expanded input limit only to images and retain the configured attachment limit.
